purpose: Probe Ubuntu yq as a zero-cost generic YAML-to-JSON capability for the live workflow audit.

steps.command:
set -euo pipefail
VER=$(apt-cache policy yq | awk '/Candidate:/ {print $2}')
test -n "$VER" && test "$VER" != '(none)'
SHA=$(apt-cache show "yq=$VER" | awk '/^SHA256:/ {print $2; exit}')
test ${#SHA} -eq 64
sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends "yq=$VER" >/dev/null
OUT=$(mktemp)
yq '.' .github/workflows/astra-shared-runtime.yml > "$OUT"
python - "$OUT" "$VER" "$SHA" <<'PY'
import json,pathlib,sys
p=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); data=json.loads(p.read_text())
assert data['name']=='ASTRA Shared Runtime Mission'
assert 'on' in data
assert 'jobs' in data and 'run-mission' in data['jobs']
print(json.dumps({'package':'yq','version':sys.argv[2],'archive_sha256':sys.argv[3],'workflow_name':data['name'],'job_ids':sorted(data['jobs'])},sort_keys=True))
print('YQ_YAML_JSON_SUPPLIER_VERIFIED')
PY
